title: Good Agricultural Practices for Sustainable Farming
reason: Provides a comprehensive overview of good agricultural practices, highlighting how they ensure food safety and promote sustainable farming.

tasks.task: Explain the core concept and benefits of Good Agricultural Practices (GAPs).

subtasks.text: Define GAPs and explain how they create safe and wholesome food for consumers or further processing.
Mention the Food and Agricultural Organization's (FAO) GAP and how it utilizes a collection of principles for on-farm and post-production processes.

tasks.task: Describe how the U.S. Department of Agriculture's GAP program operates.

subtasks.text: Describe the U.S. Department of Agriculture Agricultural Marketing Service's audit and certification program for farms using good and good handling practices.

tasks.task: Discuss the objectives of increasing small-holder productivity through good agricultural practices.

subtasks.text: Explain how increasing the demand for agricultural crops to double as the world's population grows will require increased GAPs and effective input use.

tasks.task: Detail the specific practices for soil management as part of GAPs.

subtasks.text: Describe reducing soil erosion through hedging and ditching and applying fertilizers at appropriate moments.
Explain maintaining soil organic content through manure application and crop rotation.

tasks.task: Outline water management practices as part of GAPs.

subtasks.text: Describe scheduling irrigation based on plant needs and soil water reserve status.
Explain maintaining soil salinity and avoiding crops with high water requirements in low availability regions.

tasks.task: Highlight animal production, health, and welfare practices under GAPs.

subtasks.text: List key elements of animal well-being under GAPs, such as freedom from hunger, pain, and disease.
Describe minimizing nontherapeutic use of antibiotics and avoiding harmful feeding practices.
